findings.message: Record lastCheckpointGC only after successful cleanup. It now advances before GC runs, so listing or deletion failures suppress retries until the GC interval elapses. Restore error propagation from GarbageCollectCheckpoints and update the timestamp only on success.
findings.evidence: recommender.go:158-160 updates the timestamp unconditionally. cluster_feeder.go:294-310 logs listing errors and returns; lines 323-325 log deletion errors without returning failure to the caller. The default GC interval is ten minutes (config.go:116), whereas the previous code preserved the timestamp on errors.

findings.message: Start a separate GC timeout after checkpoint writing finishes. Both operations now receive the deadline created before writing, so writing can exhaust GC's budget before cleanup starts. Under sustained writing pressure, due GC attempts can repeatedly receive an expired context.
findings.evidence: RunOnce creates one deadline at recommender.go:190-192. MaintainCheckpoints sequentially passes that same context to StoreCheckpoints (line 156) and GC (line 160). checkpoint_writer.go:114-118 checks cancellation only after processing a VPA, and line 134 waits for workers, allowing writing to finish after the deadline. GC passes the inherited context to checkpoint Delete calls at cluster_feeder.go:323. Previously, its timeout started after StoreCheckpoints returned.

result.coverage: Reviewed TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, all changed production hunks, configuration wiring, controller scheduling, GC failure paths, and checkpoint writer cancellation behavior. Challenged both findings against the actual caller flow and kept them distinct: failure retry bookkeeping and independent operation deadlines.
limitations: Read-only source inspection only; no tests were run.
Generated clients, checkpoint API helper implementations, and external callers are unavailable; exact request cancellation behavior and downstream deployment effects were not verified.
result.contribution: Established two contract violations from staged source. Confirmed that moving the write deadline to RunOnce preserves its start point for the supplied caller; the evidenced timeout regression is sharing that deadline with subsequent GC. Accounted for workers checking cancellation after processing rather than assuming writing stops exactly at expiry.
